detail:
Full summary: Built a record-content analyzer for the benchmark harness: scores .twining/ store record QUALITY (rationale authored vs derived, alternatives with real reasons, scope, affected files) instead of tool-call names
Decisions: Chose to ship the content scorer as a standalone cross-cutting analyzer rather than a scenario dimension folded into the CES composite — the product's open question is whether record richness PREDICTS better outcomes, which is a correlation between capture quality and work quality; making capture quality a component of the composite would make 'richer records produce higher composite' true by arithmetic rather than by evidence, destroying the ability to test the hypothesis. Secondary reasons: adding a fifth weighted dimension shifts every historical number and breaks comparability with the n=16 pooled result, and the hard constraint forbids changing the instrument and adding to it in the same change.; Chose to score conditions with no .twining/ store as N/A (applicable false, value null) rather than zero — scoring baseline and shared-markdown zero would conflate 'no coordination substrate' with 'bad records' and would make the dimension a twining-detector, which is exactly the defect the decision-documentation scorer had. Rejected alternative: score shared-markdown's COORDINATION.md through an equivalent markdown extractor — reason_rejected: an NL parser that recovers 60 percent of rationale from markdown and 100 percent from a JSON field manufactures a 40-point advantage for Twining out of pure instrument asymmetry, the same class of artifact in new clothes; it needs human-labelled validation first.; Chose a MEAN of per-decision quality with de-duplication on normalised summary as the volume defence, rather than any coverage or count term — a mean makes adding records neutral unless the records are good, and padding good work with stubs strictly lowers the score; de-duplication closes the only remaining route, writing one excellent record ten times. Volume is reported as coverage counts but never blended in.; Chose to EXCLUDE commit linkage from the rubric despite it being a proposed signal — reason: commit_hashes is empty on every decision in every recorded run because benchmark agents do not commit, the harness auto-commits between sessions under its own message, so the term would be constant zero across all conditions and would depress every score while discriminating nothing. The count is still reported as coverage.commitLinkedCount so the exclusion stays auditable.; Chose to exclude contradiction detection and score only supersession USAGE as a reported diagnostic — reason: detecting contradiction between decision pairs needs semantic comparison, which regexes do unreliably and an LLM judge does expensively and non-deterministically while importing the judge's biases into what is meant to be a mechanical instrument.; Chose to treat records read from a v1 decisions/index.json as sourceKind index-projection whose rationale and alternatives terms return null (unmeasurable) rather than zero, renormalising the remaining weights — reason: the projection shape structurally has no rationale or alternatives field, so an empty value there is an artifact of the capture, not evidence the agent wrote nothing. Gated on source SHAPE not on field absence, so a full record that omits its rationale still scores zero.; Chose to add an explicit measuredWeight field to the score result — reason: a store of summary projections can legitimately read 100 on the two terms that survived while saying nothing about rationale, and a bare 100 invites exactly the misreading the dimension exists to prevent.; Chose to add a durable store snapshot step (DataCollector.saveTwiningStoreSnapshot) called from the orchestrator before teardown, rather than leaving the analyzer unrunnable — reason: the Twining conditions delete workingDir/.twining in doTeardown and the target then deletes the working dir, and .twining paths are filtered out of transcript.fileChanges, so nothing survives a run for a post-hoc analyzer to read. The step is read-only with respect to the store, writes only a new file, and is wrapped so it can never throw and cost a paid run.; Chose to verify test discrimination by systematic mutation rather than the project's standard git stash push src/ check — reason: stashing a NEW module removes the file entirely so every test dies on an import error, which makes a test that pins nothing look identical to one that pins everything. Fifteen targeted mutations were applied one at a time and all fifteen were caught by the intended test.
Findings: warning: the benchmark's .twining/ store does not survive a run — twining-default.ts:78 and twining-full delete workingDir/.twining in doTeardown, orchestrator.ts:568 deletes the working dir, and data-collector.ts:198 filters .twining/ out of transcript.fileChanges. Verified empty infrastructureFileChanges across all 120 recorded transcripts in run 4640f3a3 and zero git-diff.patch files mentioning .twining. Closed by adding saveTwiningStoreSnapshot before teardown.; warning: the .twining/ path pattern recently added to scoreDecisionDocumentation in src/scenarios/conflict-resolution.ts is dead code — it is tested against transcriptC.fileChanges, which by construction never contains a .twining/ path because data-collector filters them into infrastructureFileChanges. The twining_record tool-call branch of that same fix does work, so no score is wrong, but the file-path half pins nothing. NOT fixed here — the task forbade modifying existing scorers.; warning: src/conditions/twining-default.ts:86-92 and twining-full.ts:81-90 snapshot v1-only store paths (.twining/blackboard.jsonl, .twining/decisions/index.json). Under the twining-mcp@2.6.0 pin a fresh benchmark working dir resolves to the sqlite backend, which mirrors to .twining/records/decisions/*.json and never creates those v1 files — so every future run's coordination-artifacts.json will be empty for Twining. Left unfixed; the new snapshot step reads both layouts and is unaffected.; The historical dataset cannot answer the rationale question at all. The only durable capture in recorded runs is coordination-artifacts.json, which preserved .twining/decisions/index.json — a summary projection with NO rationale and NO alternatives fields. Reconstructed and scored: twining-default value=100 measuredWeight=0.40, twining-full value=92 measuredWeight=0.40, both with rationale=null and alternatives=null. The 100/92 split reflects scope specificity and file population only and must not be compared to a future fully-measured store.; The real-data check caught a defect the synthetic unit tests missed: the alternatives term returned 0 rather than null for index projections, silently zeroing 25 percent of the rubric weight on every historical record. The fixtures did not catch it because I had written them to match my own assumption. Running a new scorer against real recorded data before trusting it is worth the ten minutes.; need: the rubric weights (0.35/0.25/0.20/0.20), the 0.5 unknown-provenance credit, the 0.4 alternative-naming floor and the 8-character reason threshold are judgement, not calibration. Nothing yet establishes that a store scoring 80 helps a later agent more than one scoring 60. The honest next step is to capture snapshots on the next paid run and correlate fully-measured content scores against the existing composite before defending the weights.
